first_impression.reaction: James Googled this because the ring is sitting in a drawer and we have a trip coming up. The intro gets to the point fast and doesn't gush: 'Engagement ring insurance is not automatic.' That's the bit we needed to hear. The travel angle in the second paragraph is why we kept going, since that's our real situation. No fairytale language, which is a relief.

journey.quote: Travel insurance often limits what it pays for each item, and theft from checked baggage or of something left unattended is commonly excluded.
journey.reaction: Useful straight away. I'd honestly assumed our travel policy would cover it. This is the gap we were worried about.

journey.quote: This is general information, not financial advice. Read the policy wording, the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS), before you buy.
journey.reaction: As a lawyer I appreciate that they aren't pretending to be an insurer. It makes everything that follows feel more credible.

journey.section: What to check in any policy
journey.quote: Every point below is a question to put to your insurer, not a statement of what any particular policy does.
journey.reaction: Honest, but by the fourth 'check your policy' it gets a bit circular. The question table helps make up for it. That table is the thing I'd actually screenshot.

journey.section: Receipt, grading report and an independent valuation
journey.quote: A laboratory grading report describes the stone (clarity, colour, cut, carat, fluorescence, polish and symmetry) but gives no value.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. We have the GIA cert and assumed that was enough. Specific and useful.

journey.quote: The ring box is the hardest object to hide and the easiest to leave behind on a sun lounger. Keep it on you.
journey.reaction: This reads like someone who has actually seen it go wrong. It's the kind of insider detail I look for.

journey.section: Travelling to your destination wedding with the rings
journey.quote: By the wedding, there are usually three rings travelling: the engagement ring and two wedding bands.
journey.reaction: Hadn't thought of that at all. Good practical point that ties the topic back to the wedding.

journey.section: Carry-on, travel dates and hotel safes
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, so the logistics around the rings sit inside one plan.
journey.reaction: Feels a bit bolted on. A planner doesn't insure my ring, so the link is thin. And 'single point of contact' is what every planner says. What does it actually mean for us day to day?

journey.section: If a ring is stolen overseas
journey.quote: The Australian Government cannot help with an insurance claim or replace anything other than a passport.
journey.reaction: Blunt and useful. Exactly the sort of thing nobody tells you until it's too late.

journey.quote: A simple band for those days, with the engagement ring in the safe, takes that risk off the table.
journey.reaction: Practical. I'd forward this bit to my mum, who keeps telling me to take it off at the beach.

journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor will plan the venue and the travel with you from first idea to the last dance, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
journey.reaction: 'Quoting in AUD' actually lands, because currency surprises are one of our biggest worries. 'From first idea to the last dance' is a little greeting-card though.

unanswered_questions: Does a Wedded Advisor actually do anything about the rings and valuables at the wedding (safe storage on the day, who holds the bands), or was that just a link to the service?
What does 'single point of contact' look like in practice: one named person, how often do we hear from them, who is on the ground on the day?
Does quoting in AUD mean we carry no currency risk on vendor payments overseas?

turn_offs_found.quote: from first idea to the last dance
turn_offs_found.why: A small cliché in an otherwise plain, grown-up piece. Not a deal-breaker, but it's the one line that sounds like marketing.

would_share_with: Partner (the policy questions table and the valuation section)
Mum (the beach and plain band tip)

cta_reaction.quote: See [how a Wedded Advisor plans the wedding travel](/wonderland-concierge).
cta_reaction.why: The article earned some trust, so I might click out of curiosity, especially with 'quoting in AUD' at the end. But I came here for ring insurance, not a planner, and the bridge from rings to the Advisor is thin. I wouldn't enquire off this post alone. I'd need to see a couple of destination posts and a real wedding first.

top_3_changes: Make the Wedded Advisor paragraph earn its place with one concrete ring-related thing an Advisor does (for example, who looks after the bands on the day), rather than a generic 'single point of contact' line.
Swap 'from first idea to the last dance' for something plain; the rest of the piece is refreshingly cliché-free.
Cut a couple of the repeated 'check your policy' lines in the policy section and let the question table carry that message.
